panel: Chua Lee Ming J (Judge of the High Court)
James Allsop IJ (International Judge, delivering the judgment)

event_log.event: Final Award rendered in Pittsburgh by 3-member panel
Singapore court grants ex parte enforcement order HC/ORC 1222/2025
Defendants file Summons 777/2025 to set aside on Grounds 1-4
Hearing before Chua J, Thorley IJ, Allsop IJ
Judgment reserved and delivered: application allowed in part

grounds.label: Public policy (spoliation/fraud)
grounds.defendants_assertion: Franchisor destroyed/concealed evidence; Award contrary to public policy

grounds.label: Natural justice (failed to address argument)
grounds.defendants_assertion: Tribunal failed to apply its mind to the 'take back Singapore' adverse-inference argument
grounds.court_finding: DKT v DKU 4-condition framework not satisfied — argument not properly before Tribunal as separate issue, not essential, considered, no prejudice

grounds.label: Outside scope of submission (damages)
grounds.defendants_assertion: Damages claim in Post-Hearing Brief was new and unpleaded
grounds.court_finding: Damages alternative was within the pleadings (COD v COE); strike-out properly refused

grounds.label: Outside scope / natural justice on Order 3 specific performance
grounds.defendants_assertion: Specific-performance Order 3 was outside submission and breached natural justice
grounds.court_finding: Tribunal was authorised to fashion a just regime to enforce cl 13.4; but on sub-paragraphs (d)(ii), (d)(iii), (f) the parties were deprived of an opportunity to be heard on the specific terms

human_findings: Tribunal had jurisdiction over the substantive dispute (Franchise Agreements containing arbitration clauses).
The Final Award did not fall foul of Singapore public policy on the spoliation issue: the Tribunal made findings against Mr Wong on the evidence.
The DKT v DKU 4-condition framework for 'infra petita' challenges was not made out.
The damages alternative was within the pleadings under COD v COE — strike-out properly refused.
The Tribunal was free to fashion a just regime to enforce cl 13.4 specifically and could go beyond a yes/no answer.
But three sub-paragraphs of Order 3 were not put to the parties for submission on their specific terms (paras 103-105), and so the order is varied to remove (d)(ii), (d)(iii) and (f).

court_orders_para_185.(a): Application set aside HC/ORC 1222/2025 allowed in part as set out in (b) and (c) below; otherwise dismissed.
court_orders_para_185.(b): HC/ORC 1222/2025 varied so that Order 3(d)(ii), Order 3(d)(iii) and Order 3(f) of the Final Award are not enforced.
court_orders_para_185.(c): The orders of the Tribunal otherwise set out in para 752 of the Final Award be enforced.
court_orders_para_185.(d-f): Costs schedule and submissions to follow within 14 days; costs to be decided on the papers if parties agree.

fact_summary: GNC Holdings (US franchisor) obtained a Final Award in Pittsburgh against its Singapore franchisee ONI Global and its related company LAC Global, including specific-performance orders requiring assignment of 54 retail leases. GNC obtained ex parte enforcement in Singapore (HC/ORC 1222/2025). The defendants applied to set aside under Singapore IAA s 31 on four grounds: public policy, natural justice, scope of submission (damages), and scope/natural justice (specific performance). The SICC dismissed three of the four grounds in full but allowed Ground 4 in part: the Tribunal was authorised to fashion a just regime to enforce the post-termination covenant, but did not afford the parties a meaningful opportunity to make submissions on three specific sub-paragraphs of Order 3, which are excised. The award is enforced as varied.
